Stability of the steady state of Pimpl() as a constraint

Source: R/constraintStability.R
constraintStability.Rd

A term of the objective that keeps the steady state of a Pimpl() stable. For every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of the Jacobian of the right-hand side at the steady state, on the manifold of the conserved quantities, it adds \(w\, r^2\) with \(r = \max(0, \mathrm{Re}\,\lambda - \lambda_0) / (\lambda_{tol} - \lambda_0)\): nothing while every real part lies below the onset \(\lambda_0\), and the weight \(w\) for each eigenvalue, both of a complex pair, whose real part reaches \(\lambda_{tol}\), the stabilityTol of pSS. Steady states that agree in all inputs count once. The gradient is exact, the Hessian Gauss-Newton.

Usage

constraintStability(
  pSS,
  p = NULL,
  onset = NULL,
  duration = NULL,
  weight = 100,
  attrName = "stability"
)

Arguments

pSS

A parfn of Pimpl(), built with deriv2 = TRUE.

p

The parfn whose output pSS reads, or NULL where pSS reads the parameters of the objective.

onset

\(\lambda_0\), below stabilityTol. NULL (default) for stabilityTol - 1 / duration: the term begins where a perturbation of the steady state decays more slowly than the data last.

duration

The time the data span, for the default onset.

weight

\(w\), the value of the term where the real part of an eigenvalue reaches stabilityTol, in units of \(-2 \log L\). Default 100.

attrName

Name of the attribute that holds the value of the term, default "stability".

Value

An objfn of the parameters of p, or of pSS without p, to add to the objective.

Details

The term is an assumption of the model, that the system rests where the steady state is taken, not data: profile() with stop = "data" and likelihood ratios read the data term without it. Parameters of p that the evaluation does not give, such as random effects, enter at 0.

Where pSS requires a stable root, an evaluation beyond stabilityTol fails. With Pimpl(controlsPTC = list(stability = FALSE)) it returns the unstable root there, and the term goes on rising.

See also

Pimpl(), constraintL2()

Examples

# \donttest{
# The Brusselator rests at x = a, y = b / a, stable while b < 1 + a^2
f <- c(x = "a - (b + 1) * x + x^2 * y", y = "b * x - x^2 * y")
old <- setwd(tempdir())
pSS <- Pimpl(f, deriv2 = TRUE, modelname = "brusselator_ss")
p <- P(c(a = "exp(la)", b = "exp(lb)"), modelname = "brusselator_p")
compile(pSS, p, output = "brusselator")
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC]
stab <- constraintStability(pSS, p, onset = -0.5, weight = 10)
# far from the Hopf point nothing, near it the term with gradient, beyond it the term on the
# unstable steady state
stab(c(la = 0, lb = log(0.5)))$value
#> [1] 0
stab(c(la = 0, lb = log(1.8)))
#> value
#> ==================
#> 12.8
#> gradient[1:2] (full length = 2)
#> ==================
#>    la    lb 
#> -64.0  57.6 
#> 
#> hessian[1:2,1:2]
#> ==================
#>      la     lb
#> la  160 -144.0
#> lb -144  129.6
#> 
#> 
#> attributes
#> ==================
#>  stability  12.8
stab(c(la = 0, lb = log(2.5)))$value
#> [1] 45
setwd(old)
# }
